ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder. Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider. Proto-Indo-European *h₁pi Proto-Germanic *bi Proto-West Germanic *bī Old English bī Middle English by English by From Middle English by, bi, from Old English bī (“by; near; around”), from Proto-West Germanic *bī, from Proto-Germanic *bi (“near; by; around; about”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁epi. Cognate with West Frisian by (“by; near”), Afrikaans by (“at; by; near”), Saterland Frisian bie (“near; by”), Dutch bij (“near; by”), German Low German bi (“by; near; at”), German bei (“by; near; at”).

ex: The mailbox is by the bus stop.

senses.d: From one side of something to the other, passing close by; past.
ex: The stream runs by our back door.
He ran straight by me.

senses.d: Not later than (the given time); not later than the end of (the given time interval); before.
ex: Be back by ten o'clock!
We'll find someone by the end of March.

senses.d: After a given amount of time has elapsed or a given event has occurred.
ex: By February, we were all sick of the cold.
By the time I realized I had left my phone at home, I was already two blocks from work.
The matter was decided by the chairman.
The boat was swamped by the water.
There was a call by the unions for a 30% pay rise.
I was aghast by what I saw.
In other directions the fields and sky were so much of one colour by the snow that it was difficult in a hasty glance to tell whereabouts the horizon occurred […].

senses.d: Indicates the creator of a work: Existing through the authorship etc. of.
ex: There are many well-known plays by William Shakespeare

senses.d: Indicates a means of achieving something: Involving/using the means of.
ex: I'd know you anywhere by your gravelly voice.
I avoided the guards by moving only when they weren't looking.

senses.d: Indicates an authority according to which something is done.
ex: By the power vested in me, I now pronounce you man and wife.
I live by my own code of ethics.

senses.d: Along a path which runs past someone or something.
ex: I watched the parade as it passed by.
There was a shepherd close by.

senses.d: To or at a place, as a residence or place of business.
ex: I'll stop by on my way home from work.
We're right near the lifeguard station. Come by before you leave.
The women spent much time after harvest putting jams by for winter and spring.

senses.d: Beyond or past a certain point.
ex: I'll somehow manage to get by.

senses.d: Out of the way, off to one side.
ex: a by path; a by room
by catch; a by issue
